item.title: 266 days deployed: USS Abraham Lincoln to return home amid rising scrutiny over sailor welfare
item.description: After an extended deployment, the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier is making its way home. While Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao minimized reports of sailor difficulties and supply deficiencies, the Navy contends that allegations regarding a mental health crisis aboard are overstated. This lengthy deployment highlights the pressures faced by the US Navy's carrier fleet, with the USS George Washington set to take over its operations in the Middle East.

item.title: Organisms living inside the gut of psychopaths could be the drivers of bad, sinful behaviour and conduct, claim scientists
item.description: Recent research indicates a potential connection between gut microorganisms and psychopathic traits. The study unveiled variations in gut and oral bacteria among individuals with differing psychopathy scores. Notably, metabolic byproducts such as glucose and taurine reflected distinct patterns across participant groups. These findings suggest a fascinating interplay between gut health and psychological characteristics, warranting further investigation to clarify these complex gut-brain interactions.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Newfoundland is on the verge of losing it's forests, all because of 11,000 moose who can't stop eating
item.description: Introduced to Newfoundland more than a century ago as a food source, moose have surged in numbers, drastically altering the island’s forest ecosystem. The absence of natural predators allows these massive herbivores to devour young trees at alarming rates. To mitigate this issue and safeguard habitats, hunting quotas are thoughtfully managed, seeking to achieve a harmony between ecological integrity and human needs.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: China's new solar plant made with 15,927 mirrors will power 50,000 homes while saving 60,000 tons of coal annually
item.description: China has proudly completed the construction of the world's tallest solar thermal power plant at an impressive altitude of over 15,000 feet. Known as the Tushuo facility, this 100 MW powerhouse utilizes mirrors to effectively concentrate solar energy onto molten salts. The resulting stored heat will generate electricity even after sunset, ultimately supplying power to approximately 50,000 households each year once connected to the grid.

item.title: 7.7 magnitude earthquake hits Indonesia: 38 killed, buildings collapse; 5 visuals of devastation
item.description: A significant earthquake registering 7.7 on the Richter scale rocked eastern Indonesia early Saturday, claiming the lives of at least thirty-eight individuals and leading to the destruction of various structures. Ongoing rescue missions are striving to aid the affected population, while landslides and widespread power failures hinder relief efforts in some areas. Although a tsunami alert was briefly raised, it was later cancelled after confirming that sea conditions were stable.

item.title: UK searches for homes with air conditioning jump 104% as heatwaves intensify
item.description: Searches for homes with air conditioning in the UK have more than doubled this summer. Repeated heatwaves prompt buyers to pay greater attention to property cooling capabilities. Many households are making practical changes to keep cool during hotter weather. Britain's housing stock faces concerns about coping with increasingly hotter summers. This shift influences buyer priorities and what they are willing to purchase.

item.title: In 1958, 58 pigs were removed from Clipperton, helping seabirds grow to 137,000
item.description: Feral pigs introduced to Clipperton Island devastated seabird populations and land crabs. Ornithologist Kenneth Stager removed fifty-eight pigs, allowing the ecosystem to gradually recover. This removal helped the seabird colony grow from 650 to over 137,000 birds. Later, black rats arrived, impacting the island's vegetation and bird populations negatively. Clipperton's story highlights invasive species' profound ecological effects on islands.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Jellyfish became a threat to France's Gravelines plant after clogging cooling systems
item.description: In a striking environmental incident, a massive jellyfish swarm has compelled the shutdown of reactors at France's Gravelines nuclear plant. The clogged seawater cooling systems have brought significant disruption to power generation. Following a related incident in 2025, the plant introduced enhanced monitoring and fishing strategies. This occurrence underscores the vulnerabilities faced by coastal nuclear installations amidst the challenges posed by extreme summer temperatures affecting France's nuclear output.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: The ground beneath Poland's wind turbines became nesting grounds for wild bees
item.description: In Poland, the bases of wind turbines have emerged as surprising havens for pollinators. Research highlights that these zones foster a thriving community of wild bees and a variety of plant species. The bare gravel and low maintenance create perfect nesting sites for ground-nesting bees. While butterflies opt for grasslands, both flies and grasslands flourish equally in these overlooked yet vital habitats for biodiversity on farmland.
